instructions.content: Reproduction is a verification exercise, not a sales pitch.
Record what you observe: quote actual output, not what the README says the output should be.
Mark every figure taken from the README or paper with (as reported); NEVER blend reported and verified numbers without distinguishing them.
Partial is better than fabricated: if only some scenarios run, record those honestly and set outcome to partially-verified.
Document the environment: OS, primary runtime version and, for a vendored submodule, the pinned commit SHA.
Confirm the slug with the user and locate the reference file (references/<slug>.md) and analysis file (analysis/ANALYSIS-<slug>.md) if they exist.
NEVER skip the existing repro check: search benchmarks/sources/ for <slug>-repro.md and, if found, report it and ask whether to re-run or update in place.

Locate the benchmark harness from the analysis file's Stage 2 section first, otherwise the reference file's benchmarks section and the vendored source at tools/<slug>/, and record harness paths and invocation scripts.
Install the dependencies the harness requires before running it.
NEVER suppress harness errors: capture stdout and stderr, quote errors verbatim, and set outcome to failed if the harness cannot complete.
Categorise each metric: Verified (within plus or minus 10 per cent of the reported value), Not reproduced (differs materially, quote both) or Could not test (unavailable infra, note why).
Create benchmarks/sources/<slug>-repro.md from assets/templates/REPRO-benchmark.yaml, with all required frontmatter fields and the four required sections.
NEVER omit YAML frontmatter: open the file with a --- block containing all required fields before any prose.
Set outcome to one of verified, partially-verified, unverified or failed, using the meanings in the skill.
Back-fill the analysis file: if Stage 2.2 does not yet reference the repro file, add a pointer with the outcome.
Run ./scripts/validate-repro-benchmark.sh on the repro file and report what was verified, what was not, and caveats about fixtures and environment.
Do not use this skill on a subject that has not been triaged; run triage-tool or triage-paper first.
If the benchmark needs live external services or paid APIs that are unavailable, set outcome to unverified and document the blocker.
When figures must be looked up from the original paper, prefer the semantic-scholar or google-scholar MCP servers over WebFetch.
Document environmental effects on results: cold-start overhead, fixture quality and dependency versions.
